name: Unterholz
prior: Mixtur-Trautonium (Trautwein 1930 / Sala): subharmonic dividers from a master oscillator plus parallel formant filters, ribbon with portamento and 'Schlagwerk' percussion (VS: trautoniks.de/com/history.html = hardware rebuilds 1990-2012; no software mentioned). Quilcom 'Trout': free Windows VST 'Trautonium simulation' with softened sawtooth, subharmonics and formant filters, presets, Windows only (VS: plugins4free.com/plugin/3284). Doepfer A-113 Subharmonic Generator: four dividers 1..24 from a pulse input, sawtooth outputs, mixtures/presets, built after Sala's design (V: doepfer.de/a113.htm; VS: modulargrid.net/e/doepfer-a-113-subharmonic-generator); Doepfer A-104 Trautonium Formant Filter: four parallel resonant filters 50 Hz-5 kHz, BP/LP (VS: manualsdir.com Doepfer A-104 manual). Moog Subharmonicon (2020): two VCOs each with two subharmonic oscillators (divisors 1-16), polyrhythm sequencers, undertone chords (A: well known, not in the search results). Avid DUC thread 2017: no Trautonium plugin or Reaktor ensemble found by the community (VS: duc.avid.com/archive/index.php/t-388474.html). Myzel: Nebel (detuned saws + sine sub f/2 + lowpass, APP 3531-3568), Obertöne (harmonic spotlight), Tiefe (folded sub). Not found: a touch/phone instrument where finger height opens the undertone mixture note by note through fixed formants, with the ribbon portamento and Sala's plucked Schlagwerk on a sequencer lane.
costNotes: Native, no worklet needed: 5 oscillators (1 osc + 1 gain measured 0.09, R: webaudio.md section 4) ~0.35, 2 bandpass biquads 0.12, ~7 gains 0.21, detune bus connections free -> ~0.7-0.8 at L1; idea's own 0.9 is conservative. L3 (two masters +-4 ct L/R, six subs, third formant, A.uni link) ~1.5. Phase lock (A, from the spec): OscillatorNodes started at the same t with frequencies f/n, glided with the same relative automation and detuned by the same cents from v.mod keep their phase integrals in exact ratio; float drift over a note is negligible, so no divider processor is needed. Square f/n for n >= 4 as triangle is right (square f/4 puts odd harmonics at f/4, 3f/4, 5f/4 ... = a dense comb below f). Burst: filter envelope on the formant BQs (frequency and Q automation) + burstEnv is 4 extra automation events per hit - trivial.
soundHeld: Distinct from Nebel only as long as the undertones are heard as a locked chord, not as thickness: at y 0 it is 'saw through two formants' (= a Nebel/Obertöne cousin), the identity arrives from y ~0.3 upward when f/2 and f/3 enter. Two consequences (A): (1) the sum of locked squares at f/2 and f/3 has period 6/f, so the ear takes f/6 as the root of a minor chord (f/6:f/5:f/4 = 10:12:15, the minor triad the pitch claims; 'moll' as listed [1,1/2,1/3,1/4,1/5] lacks the 1/6 that completes it - add it or drop the claim); the finger's note is then the TOP voice of a chord whose root lies 2.5 octaves down. On a bass column (55 Hz) the root is 9 Hz: the mixture must be capped by f (drop n with f/n < ~35 Hz) or the top of the field is mud. (2) Height staggering y_n with smoothstep width 0.2 gives audible 'steps' while sliding the finger vertically - that is the Trautonium's switchable mixtures and is a feature, but Höhe via tilt (Gestik) then plays a staircase, not a sweep; keep the steps but give the formants a continuous rise so something moves between steps. Formants at fixed 450/1800 Hz x 2^(0.5y) on a saw are vocal ('ah'-'eh'); with Q 4 they are mild - the Sala sound needs Q 6-10 and a little drive into the filters (A-104 users distort its inputs, VS). Bebung on the detune bus moves all oscillators in cents = clean ribbon vibrato. Portamento across columns through locked subs = the Trautonium glide; works with v.glide as in Nebel.
soundBurst: Sala's Schlagwerk is credible: a 3 ms attack, Q jump and a one-octave formant drop give a woody 'bong' because the locked low squares carry the body; with gate x 0.5 and rel 0.3 s it sits between Membran and Kalimba in the Puls. Failure: with mixtur open at the lane's Höhe the hit is a chord-stab (five oscillators), which on four lanes with sixteenths becomes a cluster wash; the lane should use only n <= 3 unless its Höhe is high. A second failure is the attack: five oscillators all starting at phase 0 at t produce a click-free but identical onset every hit (no randomness) - fine for a machine lane, add 2-5 cents of per-hit detune of the master for life.
failureModes: Nebel-adjacent at low Höhe: saw + lowpass/formant is ordinary; the engine only earns its place from y ~0.3 up - set default y_n lower (n=2 at 0.05) so the first sub is always present
Undertone root 2.5 octaves below the finger: on low columns (f < 80 Hz) f/4..f/6 are sub-audible mud; cap the mixture by absolute frequency (~35 Hz)
'moll' mixture as listed [1,1/2,1/3,1/4,1/5] does not contain the f/4:f/5:f/6 minor triad claimed; add 1/6 (or use Sala's [1,1/2,1/3,1/5,1/6])
Staircase under Gestik: smoothstep steps of 0.2 in y make tilt a 4-step switch; keep the steps (Trautonium mixtures) but run the formant rise continuously
Formants at Q 4 and no drive are too polite for the Trautonium's nasal bite; Q 6-10 and a soft WaveShaper ('none') before the filters, 2x only at L3
Chord stabs on a Puls lane pile up into clusters at high density; limit lanes to n <= 3 by default
Burst onset identical every hit (all oscillators at phase 0); randomise master detune 2-5 ct per hit
Undertone pitches fall outside the scale (wanted) but confuse the Tonstufen-snap and 'alle Töne' Gestik features that read the voice's f; document that f is the top voice
verdict: Rare, not new: the subharmonic-mixture-plus-formant recipe is the Mixtur-Trautonium, available as Doepfer A-113/A-104 hardware, Moog's Subharmonicon and the free Windows-only Quilcom 'Trout'; no phone or touch instrument puts the mixture under the finger's height with Sala's Schlagwerk on a sequencer lane. Native and cheap (~0.8 units, L3 ~1.5), phase lock comes for free from shared-clock oscillators. Held it is only distinct once the undertones are open, so the first sub should enter almost immediately and the mixture must be capped by absolute frequency on bass columns, where the implied root (f/6) drops below 20 Hz; the listed 'moll' set also lacks the 1/6 that makes its promised minor triad. The Puls 'bong' is the strongest part; keep lanes to three partials or four lanes turn to cluster mud. Worth building, with the caveat that at low Höhe it is a Nebel cousin.
